Subject: Take-home: Systems Orchestration Challenge — delivery + review plan

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the next step with us — attached is the take-home packet for the Systems Orchestration Challenge (PDF attached). Key points: 

- Deadline: 72 hours from now (Fri, 2027-03-12 09:12 PT). If you need an extension, let me know ASAP.
- Deliverables: code (runnable), a short README with run instructions, a 2–3 slide PDF summarizing design choices, and a short script to reproduce the sample result.
- Submission: upload to the Hireflow submission link or reply to this thread with a .zip containing the artifacts. We prefer a single archive named lastname_firstname_submission.zip.
- Allowed languages/frameworks: Python 3.9+, Go, or Node. You may use standard ML libraries (PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow). If you plan to rely on external hosted APIs (e.g., OpenAI), note that the reviewers will need reproducible outputs — include a recorded sample and a fallback path if the API is not available.

Marissa and Lauren are on the review slate; they will check correctness, reproducibility, and infra/latency implications. If anything in the prompt is ambiguous, ask here so everyone sees the reply.

Good luck — reach out if you get blocked.

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Talent Partner, Engineering Recruiting
Redwood Inference

Hi Alex — quick answers inline.

> the challenge asks for a demo script that shows a deployed pipeline. Are we expected to actually deploy to a cloud instance, or is a local emulation acceptable?

Local emulation is fine. The primary reviewer goals are: (1) we can run your steps locally without secrets, (2) the README shows how to move to a live deployment if desired, and (3) the results are reproducible with the provided sample inputs. If you do a cloud demo, include a recorded video and clearly call out dependencies.

> I may request a short extension.

We can offer a one-time 24-hour extension on request. If you need that, reply here and I’ll update the deadline. Please note any extension must still allow reviewers enough time to evaluate before our next internal sync (we're aiming to adjudicate by Mon, 2027-03-15).

Thanks for checking — ping me if anything else pops up.

Cheers,
Dylan
